name: create-canvas
description: Create a new canvas note, empty or from a canvas document (JSON Canvas with Kanso's ink nodes), validated like any canvas.

bookId.description: The notebook ID. Without one the canvas goes to the Inbox.

canvas.description: A canvas document: {nodes: [...], edges: [...]}. Leave out for an empty canvas.

tags.description: An array of tag IDs to assign.

name: edit-canvas
description: Change a canvas with a batch of operations, applied all or none (a refused batch changes nothing). Each operation has an `op`: addNode {type: text|file|link|group|ink, x, y, width?, height?, text?, file? (a 'note:' ID or one of the canvas's 'file:' attachments), title?, url?, label?, color?, id?}, updateNode {id, text?, title?, color?, label?}, moveNode {id, x, y}, resizeNode {id, width, height}, removeNode {id} (arrows to it go too), addEdge {fromNode, toNode, fromSide?, toSide?, fromEnd?, toEnd?, label?, color?, id?}, updateEdge {id, ...}, removeEdge {id}, addStrokes {node, strokes: [{tool?, color?, width?, points: [[x, y, pressure], ...]}]} (points relative to the ink node; Kanso assigns the IDs), removeStrokes {node, strokes: [id, ...]}, moveStrokes {node, strokes: [id, ...], dx, dy}, setGroup {nodes: [id, ...], group?} (omit group to take them out of theirs), renameGroup {id, label}, rename {title}. Any operation on an existing item may carry `ifVersion` (its `kansoVersion` from `read-canvas`); the batch may carry `ifRev` (the note's `_rev`). A stale one is refused with the current versions. Works on shared canvases too, as one change the other people see arrive. Answers the new rev and the IDs the batch created.

noteId.description: The canvas note's ID, starting with 'note:'.

ifRev.description: The `_rev` you read; the batch is refused if the canvas has changed since.

name: kanso-ask-read-lines
description: Read lines of one note for Ask. Returns the lines written `L12| text`, under the note's number, so you can cite them as `[number:L12-14]`. At most 200 lines. A note that cannot be read is reported as not found.

noteId.description: ID of the note. It always starts with `note:`.

start.description: The first line to read, counting from 1.

end.description: The last line to read, counting from 1. At most 200 lines after start.

name: kanso-ask-search
description: Search the user's notes for Ask. Returns the best matching notes, each with a number, its title, the day it last changed and the lines that match, written `L12| text`. Cite what you use as `[number:L12]` or `[number:L12-14]`, with the note's number and the line numbers shown. Only notes this session may read are searched.

name: kanso-ask-when
description: Find notes by when they were written or changed, or tasks by when they are due, for Ask. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Returns numbered notes with their opening lines, written `L1| text`, and tasks due in the range with their lines.

to.description: The last day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to the first day.

kind.description: `written` finds notes changed in the range; `about` finds tasks due in it.

name: kanso-attach-file
description: Create an image attachment from base64 bytes and explicitly append its Markdown image link to a note. The file must fit Kanso’s 10 MiB attachment limit and use a supported image content type.

name.description: The filename to store and the image alt text.

contentType.description: Supported type: image/png, image/jpeg, image/jpg, image/svg+xml, image/gif, image/heic, or image/heif.

data.description: Base64 encoded file bytes, no data URI prefix.

name: kanso-create-daily-note
description: Open the daily note for a day, creating it when there is none, as Kanso's Today command does. Daily notes have fixed IDs (`note:daily-YYYY-MM-DD`) and titles (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and live in the Journal notebook (`book:journal`), which is created on first use. A new daily note is filled in from the Journal's daily template, if one is set. Returns the note's ID, title, notebook and link, and whether it was created now.

date.description: The day, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today in this computer's time zone.

name: kanso-create-from-template
description: Create a note from a template: a note in the Templates notebook (`book:templates`). The template's body is copied with its variables filled in: `{{date}}` (YYYY-MM-DD), `{{time}}` (HH:MM), `{{title}}` (the new note's title), `{{date:FORMAT}}` and `{{time:FORMAT}}` (strftime-like: %Y %m %d %e %B %b %A %a %H %M and more) and `{{cursor}}` (removed). Other text in double braces stays as it is. The note gets the template's tags and records it as `sourceTemplateId`. Returns the new note's ID, title, notebook and link.

templateId.description: ID of the template note. It can be found as `_id` in the note docs. It always starts with `note:`.

title.description: The new note's title; `{{title}}` in the template becomes it.

bookId.description: The notebook to create the note in. It can be found as `_id` in the book docs. It always starts with `book:`. Defaults to the Inbox (`book:inbox`), created on first use.

name: kanso-export-html
description: Export a note as one self-contained HTML page, as Kanso's "Export as web page" does. TeX math ($…$ and $$…$$), Mermaid diagrams and Excalidraw drawings are drawn as inline SVG, attached images are embedded as data URIs, and the page has no scripts and loads nothing from the network. Returns the HTML.

noteId.description: ID of the note to export. It can be found as `_id` in the note docs. It always starts with `note:`.

theme.description: The colors of the page: Kanso's light (paper) or dark (graphite) theme.

name: kanso-get-outline
description: Retrieve a note's outline: its headings in order, each with its level (1 to 6), its text without Markdown markers, and the 0-based line it is on in the note's body. Headings inside code blocks are not part of the outline.

noteId.description: ID of the note. It can be found as `_id` in the note docs. It always starts with `note:`.

name: kanso-get-properties
description: Read the Kanso properties parsed from a note body. The note must be visible to this caller.

noteId.description: The note ID, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-list-attachments
description: List attachment metadata for files embedded in a note. The note must be available through the local API.

noteId.description: The note ID, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-list-backlinks
description: List notes that link to this note by ID or wiki title. The target and every returned note must be visible to this caller.

noteId.description: The target note ID, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-list-mentions
description: List the lines of notes that mention a person or project page (by link, @name or plain words). Pass the page's note ID or its name or alias. The page and every returned note must be visible to this caller.

entity.description: The person or project page: its note ID (with the `note:` prefix), or its name or an alias.

name: kanso-list-note-links
description: List outgoing ID and wiki links in a note, with their source line and resolved visible target when available. The note must be visible to this caller.

noteId.description: The note ID, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-list-open-loops
description: List open loops: things notes say the writer will do ("I'll send the deck", "TODO: renew passport"), is waiting on ("waiting on Rudo"), or has to check, that are not checkboxes. Kanso finds them with phrase rules and, when the person approved them, with AI (`source` is `rule` or `ai`). Each has its sentence, kind (`mine`, `waiting` or `question`), any due date, its 0-based line in the note's body, and the note's ID, title, notebook and link. Loops the person closed or dismissed are not listed. Locked notes and notes tagged #ai-exclude have none.

book.description: Only loops in this notebook's notes. It can be found as `_id` in the book docs. It always starts with `book:`.

limit.description: Limit the number of loops returned

name: kanso-list-tags
description: List tags used by notes available to this caller. Counts include only notes the caller may see.

name: kanso-list-tasks
description: List the task-list items (`- [ ] …` and `- [x] …`) in notes outside the trash, with the note each is in. A task's due date is an `@YYYY-MM-DD` (or `@YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, which also sets a reminder) in its text. Dated tasks come first, soonest first, then tasks without a date. Each task has its text, whether it is done, its due date, its 0-based line in the note's body, and the note's ID, title, notebook and link. To tick a task off, change its `[ ]` to `[x]` on that line with patch-note.

status.description: Which tasks: open ones (not done), done ones, or all.

dueBefore.description: Only tasks due on a day before this one, as YYYY-MM-DD.

dueAfter.description: Only tasks due on a day after this one, as YYYY-MM-DD.

bookId.description: Only tasks in this notebook's notes. It can be found as `_id` in the book docs. It always starts with `book:`.

limit.description: Limit the number of tasks returned

name: kanso-list-versions
description: List saved versions of a visible note. This returns revision metadata only, not historical text.

noteId.description: The note ID, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-move-note
description: Move one note to an explicitly named notebook. The store enforces notebook and lock rules.

name: kanso-read-attachment
description: Read one attachment document embedded in a visible note, including its stored base64 bytes and metadata. Only available to the full local API caller.

fileId.description: The attachment file ID, with or without the `file:` prefix.

noteId.description: The note ID containing this attachment, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-read-version
description: Read one saved version of a currently visible note. This does not restore or change the note.

noteId.description: The note ID, with or without the `note:` prefix.

rev.description: The exact revision identifier returned by kanso-list-versions.

name: kanso-related-notes
description: Find the notes most similar in meaning to a note, by Kanso's related notes: embeddings made on the user's device from each note's words, never sent anywhere. Notes the note already links to, or is linked from, are left out. Returns each note's ID, title, `inkdrop://note/<id>` link and similarity (0 to 1, higher is closer), most similar first. Related notes are off until the user turns them on in Kanso's Settings; while they are off, or the note isn't indexed yet, it returns an empty list and says why.

noteId.description: ID of the note. It can be found as `_id` in the note docs. It always starts with `note:`.

limit.description: How many notes to return, from 1 to 20.

name: kanso-resolve-wikilink
description: Find the note a wiki-link points at. Accepts `[[Title]]`, `[[Title#Heading]]` or `[[Title|alias]]`, with or without the brackets. Titles match without regard to case or extra spaces, among notes outside the trash; when several notes share a title, the one created first is the match. Returns the note's ID, title and `inkdrop://note/<id>` link, which is the form to write when linking to it, plus the heading's line when the link names a heading the note has.

link.description: The wiki-link, such as `[[Project Plan#Budget]]`, or just the title.

name: kanso-run-query-view
description: Run the first saved `query` fenced view in a note using Kanso’s query parser and evaluator. Locked, trashed, excluded, and out-of-scope notes are omitted.

noteId.description: The note containing the saved query view, with or without the `note:` prefix.

name: kanso-search-by-meaning
description: Find the notes about something, by meaning rather than by words: the search is turned into numbers by the same language model as Kanso's related notes, on the user's device, and compared with every note's. A note can match without containing any of the words; for notes containing the words, use search-notes. Returns each note's ID, title, `inkdrop://note/<id>` link and similarity (0 to 1, higher is closer), most similar first, leaving out notes less than 0.35 similar. It needs related notes on in Kanso's Settings and the Kanso app open with its model loaded (a server started with `kanso serve` has no model); otherwise it returns an empty list and says why.

query.description: What the notes should be about, in a few words or a sentence.

limit.description: How many notes to return, from 1 to 20.

name: kanso-set-task-done
description: Set one task’s checked state by its note, current line, and exact task text. This is an explicit note write; it fails without changing the note if the task moved ambiguously.

line.description: The task’s current zero-based line in the note body.

text.description: The exact task text returned by kanso-list-tasks, including any due token.

done.description: True to tick the task, false to clear its checkbox.

name: list-canvases
description: List canvases (notes of type canvas) only, never Markdown notes. Each has its title, notebook, tags, size in bytes and a short Markdown summary of the text cards, card titles, links and recognized handwriting on it. Read the whole document with `read-canvas`. Locked canvases are not listed.

bookId.description: ID of the notebook. It always starts with 'book:'.

tagIds.description: An array of tag IDs to filter. It always starts with 'tag:'.

sort.description: Sort the canvases by the specified field

descending.description: Reverse the order of the output

limit.description: Limit the number of results returned

name: read-canvas
description: Read a canvas as JSON: its cards (nodes), arrows (edges) and ink strokes, each with its `kansoVersion`, and the note's `_rev`. Pass `groupId` to get only what lies inside one group. Stroke points are [x, y, pressure] relative to their ink node. Use the versions as `ifVersion` and `_rev` as `ifRev` in `edit-canvas` so you never overwrite drawing you have not seen.

noteId.description: The canvas note's ID, starting with 'note:'.

groupId.description: The ID of a group node on the canvas: return only the cards, strokes and arrows inside its rectangle.
